subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

How often is he praised by his teachers!

options.A: How often do his teachers praise him!
options.B: He praises his teachers so often!
options.C: He is praising his teachers so often!
options.D: How often does he praise his teachers!
options.a: How often do his teachers praise him!
options.b: He praises his teachers so often!
options.c: He is praising his teachers so often!
options.d: How often does he praise his teachers!

solution:
Rule: Passive: is + V³ + by + agent → Active: agent + V1/V5 + object. For an exclamatory/interrogative structure with 'How often', the active voice retains the interrogative structure using 'do/does'.
Explicit changes: by his teachers → His teachers (subject)

is praised → praise (simple present, plural subject)

he → him (object)

Final sentence: How often do his teachers praise him!

Option A correctly fixes the option choice to match the active voice conversion of 'How often is he praised by his teachers!'.
conceptTested: Conversion of active/passive voice for exclamatory or interrogative sentences in simple present tense.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Change the following active voice sentence into passive voice by selecting the correct option.

They will have completed the railway electrification by next year.

options.A: The railway electrification has been completed by next year.
options.B: The railway electrification will have been completed by next year.
options.C: The railway electrification will have been completing by next year.
options.D: The railway electrification will have completed by next year.
options.a: The railway electrification has been completed by next year.
options.b: The railway electrification will have been completed by next year.
options.c: The railway electrification will have been completing by next year.
options.d: The railway electrification will have completed by next year.

solution:
Rule: Future perfect active (will have + V³) → passive will have been + V³.
Explicit changes: Object 'the railway electrification' → subject The railway electrification

will have completed → will have been completed

They → dropped (a general subject is usually omitted)

by next year → unchanged

Final sentence: The railway electrification will have been completed by next year.

Option 1 changes the tense, option 3 uses 'completing', and option 4 is not passive (no 'been').
conceptTested: Future perfect tense active (will have + V3) converts to passive as 'will have been + V3'.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

The students are made to clean the classroom every day.

options.A: The teacher makes the students clean the classroom every day.
options.B: The students clean the classroom every day.
options.C: The classroom is cleaned by the students every day.
options.D: The students are cleaning the classroom every day.
options.a: The teacher makes the students clean the classroom every day.
options.b: The students clean the classroom every day.
options.c: The classroom is cleaned by the students every day.
options.d: The students are cleaning the classroom every day.

solution:
Rule: With make, the active uses a bare infinitive (make + object + V1), while the passive uses 'to' (be made + to + V1). The doer is not stated in the passive, so a suitable subject (the teacher) is supplied in the active.
Explicit changes: are made (simple present passive) → makes (simple present active, singular subject)

Doer supplied → The teacher

The students → object the students

to clean → clean ('to' is dropped after 'make' in the active)

Final sentence: The teacher makes the students clean the classroom every day.

Options 2 and 4 lose the sense of being made (forced) to clean, and option 3 is still passive.
conceptTested: Causative verb 'make' in active takes a bare infinitive (make + object + V1), while passive uses 'be made + to + V1'.

The students are made to clean the classroom every day.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.

Not a word was spoken by any of the witnesses during the trial.

options.A: Any of the witnesses did not speak a word during the trial.
options.B: None of the witnesses spoke a word during the trial.
options.C: No witnesses had spoken a word during the trial.
options.D: No witness has spoken a word during the trial.
options.a: Any of the witnesses did not speak a word during the trial.
options.b: None of the witnesses spoke a word during the trial.
options.c: No witnesses had spoken a word during the trial.
options.d: No witness has spoken a word during the trial.

solution:
Rule: Simple past passive (was + V³) → simple past active (V²). A negative passive with 'Not a word ... by any of' becomes 'None of ... + V2' in the active; starting a sentence with 'Any ... not' is incorrect.
Explicit changes: by any of the witnesses → subject None of the witnesses (the negative moves to the subject)

was spoken → spoke

Not a word → object a word

during the trial → unchanged

Final sentence: None of the witnesses spoke a word during the trial.

Option 1 wrongly begins with 'Any ... did not', option 3 changes the tense to past perfect, and option 4 changes it to present perfect.
conceptTested: Simple past passive (was + V3) converts to simple past active (V2) with appropriate negative subject handling.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

He bought a new car.

options.A: A new car was bought by him.
options.B: A new car is bought by him.
options.C: A new car has been bought.
options.a: A new car was bought by him.
options.b: A new car is bought by him.
options.c: A new car has been bought.

solution:
Rule: Simple past active → was/were + V³ in the passive.
Explicit changes: Object 'a new car' → subject

bought → was bought

He → by him

Final sentence: A new car was bought by him.

Option 2 uses the present tense, option 3 changes the tense and drops the doer, and option 4 ('had bought') is not a passive form.
conceptTested: Simple past active (V2) converts to passive using was/were + V3.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Somebody has broken the side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year.

options.A: The side lamps have been broken which were installed by the municipal corporation last year.
options.B: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.
options.C: The side lamps which were being installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.
options.D: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year had been broken.
options.a: The side lamps have been broken which were installed by the municipal corporation last year.
options.b: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.
options.c: The side lamps which were being installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.
options.d: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year had been broken.

solution:
Rule: Present perfect active $\rightarrow$ has/have been + past participle. The subject "somebody" is dropped in the passive.
Explicit changes: has broken the side lamps $\rightarrow$ the side lamps have been broken

The relative clause "which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year" stays unchanged and stays next to "side lamps".

Final sentence: The side lamps which had been installed by the municipal corporation last year have been broken.

Option 1 separates the clause from its noun and changes its tense; options 3 and 4 change the tenses.
conceptTested: Present perfect active verb 'has broken' changes to 'have been broken' in the passive voice, preserving relative clauses.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

He said that he would not tolerate such nuisance in the office.

options.A: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated had been said by him.
options.B: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.C: It had been said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.D: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerating had been said by him.
options.a: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated had been said by him.
options.b: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.c: It had been said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.
options.d: That such nuisance in the office would not be tolerating had been said by him.

solution:
Rule: For "said that ...", the passive uses It was said by + agent + that - clause; the verb inside the clause also becomes passive: would tolerate $\rightarrow$ would be tolerated.
Explicit changes: He said $\rightarrow$ It was said by him

he would not tolerate such nuisance $\rightarrow$ such nuisance would not be tolerated

Final sentence: It was said by him that such nuisance in the office would not be tolerated.

Options 1 and 3 use "had been said" (wrong tense), and option 4 uses "would not be tolerating".
conceptTested: Indirect speech sentences with 'said that' convert the main clause to 'It was said by [agent]' and the subordinate modal verb 'would tolerate' to 'would be tolerated'.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

The wife advised the husband to maintain silence when she was practising yoga.

options.A: The husband was advised to maintain silence by the wife when yoga was practised by her.
options.B: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.
options.C: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence by her when yoga was being practised.
options.D: The husband was advised to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her by the wife.
options.a: The husband was advised to maintain silence by the wife when yoga was practised by her.
options.b: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.
options.c: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence by her when yoga was being practised.
options.d: The husband was advised to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her by the wife.

solution:
Rule: Simple past $\rightarrow$ was + past participle; past continuous $\rightarrow$ was being + past participle. The infinitive "to maintain silence" stays unchanged.
Explicit changes: The wife advised the husband $\rightarrow$ The husband was advised by the wife

she was practising yoga $\rightarrow$ yoga was being practised by her

Final sentence: The husband was advised by the wife to maintain silence when yoga was being practised by her.

Option 1 uses "was practised" (wrong tense); options 3 and 4 misplace the agents.
conceptTested: Simple past tense changes to 'was/were + past participle' and past continuous tense changes to 'was/were being + past participle' in the passive voice.
